title: Thick chocolate chip cookies
description: Tall, chocolate-packed cookies with crisp golden edges and soft, chewy centers.
ingredients: 1 cold egg plus 1 cold egg yolk
steps: Cube the **cold butter**. Beat it in a bowl or stand mixer on high speed for about 2 minutes, until creamy.
Add the **brown sugar** and **granulated sugar**. Beat on high speed for 2–3 minutes, until well combined.
Add the **cold egg**, **cold egg yolk**, and **vanilla bean paste**. Mix on high speed for 3–4 minutes, until fully incorporated.
In a separate bowl, combine the **flour**, **baking powder**, **baking soda**, **cornstarch**, **salt**, and **instant coffee**.
Gradually add the dry ingredients to the **butter** mixture. Add the **chocolate chips** and **milk chocolate chunks**. Mix only until combined; do not overmix.
Scoop the dough into tall 6 oz balls on a baking sheet. Freeze for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Preheat the oven to 350°F. Place 3–4 dough balls on a prepared baking sheet, about 4 inches apart.
Bake for 16–18 minutes, until the edges are golden and crisp and the centers are soft and chewy. Let the cookies cool completely before serving.
notes: Freeze the shaped dough before baking. Leave plenty of space between the large cookies.

title: Turkish meatballs (köfte)
description: Juicy beef-and-lamb köfte with a short ingredient list and a good rest before cooking.
ingredients: 800 g beef brisket mince, ground twice
200 g lamb belly or flank mince, ground once
100 g stale soft bread, soaked in sparkling mineral water and squeezed dry
1 medium onion, grated and squeezed dry
steps: Put the prepared **beef mince**, **lamb mince**, **bread**, **onion**, **garlic**, **salt**, and **black pepper** on a tray or clean worktop with enough room to knead them. Knead for no more than 8–10 minutes.
Transfer the mixture to a container as one piece. Cover it and refrigerate for at least 2 hours. An overnight rest is even better.
Divide the cold mixture into 50–60 g portions and shape them as you like.
Cook the köfte in a pan or oven. For the oven method, place them on a parchment-lined tray and bake at 220°C in a preheated oven for about 8–12 minutes.
notes: Avoid overmixing. Warm, overworked meat can lose fat and moisture and become rubbery. The lamb adds flavor and fat; the bread helps the köfte stay juicy and hold together. The high oven heat browns the outside by the time the center cooks. The original cook prefers to let the meat flavor lead, but you can add more spices to taste.

title: Date cake
description: A tender cake sweetened with Medjool dates, with an optional date syrup icing.
ingredients: 1 cup hot coffee or hot water
1/2 cup (120 mL) avocado oil, light olive oil, or canola oil
## Optional flour substitutions — use one instead of self-rising flour
Almond flour: 2 cups (180 g) almond flour plus 1 tsp (5 g) baking powder
All-purpose flour: 1 1/2 cups (210 g) all-purpose flour plus 1 tsp (5 g) baking powder
3 tbsp date syrup or maple syrup
2 tbsp coconut milk or milk of your choice, plus more as needed
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Coat a baking pan with nonstick spray.
Put the **pitted dates** in a heatproof bowl and pour the **hot coffee or water** over them. Let them soak until soft. Let the mixture cool to lukewarm before blending.
Add the **eggs**, **oil**, softened **dates**, and all the soaking liquid to a blender. Blend for about 30 seconds, until smooth.
Add the **flour** and pulse just twice, briefly, until incorporated. If **flour** remains, fold it in gently by hand. Do not overblend; this can make the cake dense.
Pour the batter into the prepared pan and tap the pan gently on the counter twice. Bake for about 45 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. Baking time depends on the pan.

While the cake bakes, make the optional icing. Mix the **powdered sugar**, **date syrup**, and **milk** until smooth and free of lumps. It should be thick but pourable. Add more **milk** a few drops at a time if needed.
Let the cake cool completely before adding the icing. Pour it over the cake, then slice and serve.
notes: You can bake the batter in muffin tins. Reduce the baking time and check for doneness earlier.

title: Sharlotka
description: A light apple sponge cake made with four simple base ingredients.
ingredients: A little lemon juice for the apples
steps: Peel the **apples** and cut them into half-moon slices or cubes. Spread most of them in a baking pan greased with **butter** and save some for the top. If you like, toss the **apples** with **cinnamon** and a little **lemon juice**.
Make sure the **eggs** are at room temperature. Beat the **eggs** and **sugar** at the mixer's highest speed for 8–10 minutes, until the mixture grows several times in volume.
Sift the **flour** into the mixture in 2–3 additions. Fold gently with a spatula, lifting the batter from the bottom to the top.
Pour the batter over the **apples**. Arrange the reserved **apples** on top. You can also fold all the **apples** into the batter instead.
Bake in a preheated oven at 175–180°C for about 35–45 minutes, checking as it bakes.
Let the cake rest in its pan for 15 minutes. Dust with **powdered sugar** and serve.
notes: The original cake uses only eggs, sugar, flour, and apples. Cinnamon or vanilla can add flavor if you like. Room-temperature eggs and gentle folding help keep the sponge light.
